prerequisites: Knowledge of CAD methodologies to model solids

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire programming skills in different programming languages.
Acquire practical skills in preparing experimental activities, including the execution of tests and interpretation of the data obtained thereof.
Acquire a global vision of the engineering problems solving process.
To use different commercial engineering software and different programming languages to solve the proposed assignments.
Idealisation, planning, execution and analysis of the results of experimental activities necessary to accomplish/validate the proposed assignments.
Communication skills, writing of scientific documents and team work.

Integration of the principles of sustainable development reflected by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into engineering practice. This includes identification of the contribution to the environment, to the society and to the economy of the solutions proposed in the project, aiming at a more sustainable and inclusive future through projects and initiatives aligned with the SDGs.

syllabus_topics: NUMERICAL MODELLING OF ENGINEERING PROBLEMS: Implementation of codes, in a specified programming language, to solve an assignment in a specified scientific area.

EXPERIMENTAL WORK APPLIED TO ENGINEERING PROBLEMS: Execution of experimental activities, in a specified scientific area. The students have to idealise, plan, prepare and execute an experiment/proof of concept.
teaching_methods: Project-based Learning in a Research Institute
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on the technical-scientific quality of activities, including innovation, thoroughness, accomplishment of objectives, autonomy, and proactiveness. It also considers the quality of the report and presentation/public demonstration, covering content, rationale, methodology, critical analysis, clarity, rigor, posture, and creativity. A qualitative scale (A-E) is mapped to a quantitative scale (19-20 for A, 17-18 for B, etc.) and a grade below 10 results from at least one factor with an E. To be eligible for evaluation, students must complete the curricular internship/group project and submit a report of the performed activities.
